planting.note: Direct sow around last frost or start indoors 6-8 weeks earlier; press seed onto the soil surface since it needs light to germinate.

directions: Prairie Glow is a bicolor selection of brown-eyed Susan bred for warm mahogany-orange petals shading to golden yellow tips, a more vivid variation on the typical species coloring. Grow it exactly as you would the straight species: full sun to light shade, average garden soil, and consistent moisture the first season while roots establish. Like the species it behaves as a short-lived perennial or biennial and self-sows readily, so let a portion of the flower heads mature and drop seed each fall to keep the colony going. The tall, branching stems produce hundreds of small flowers over a long midsummer-to-frost bloom window that draws bees, small butterflies, and later goldfinches to the seed heads.

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring or fall in full sun and lean, sharply drained soil; foliage color is most vivid in cooler weather and fades toward solid green in summer heat.

directions: Passionate Rainbow was selected as a foliage sport of gaura and stands apart from other cultivars for its tricolor leaves, which emerge streaked cream, pink, and green before settling into a softer variegation as temperatures climb. Plant in full sun in lean, well-drained soil; like all gaura it is intolerant of soggy roots and performs best where drainage is excellent. It still produces the wiry, dancing sprays of small pink four-petaled flowers typical of the species, but many gardeners grow it as much for the season-long foliage color as for bloom. Cut back hard in midsummer if stems sprawl or lose vigor, which refreshes both foliage color and flowering for the fall.

common_name: Belleza White Gaura (Compact Uniform Seed-Grown White Gaura)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or fall in full sun and well-drained, lean soil; the companion white-flowered selection to Belleza Dark Pink in the same uniform seed-grown series.

directions: Belleza White carries the same compact, uniform, early-flowering habit bred into the Belleza seed series but with pure white, four-petaled flowers instead of pink, opening on the same slender, wiry stems that flutter in the lightest breeze. Give it full sun and lean, well-drained soil; excellent drainage is essential since gaura declines quickly wherever water stands around the crown. Bloom is nearly continuous from late spring through frost, and the tidy, mounded habit makes it a better fit for containers and small border spaces than older, looser open-pollinated gaura types. Shear back by about a third in midsummer to keep the plant compact and encourage a fresh flush of flowers into fall.

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in full sun and lean, well-drained soil; part of the Gaudi series bred for compact size and deep rose-red flower color on dark stems.

directions: Gaudi Red is a compact gaura selection prized for its dark burgundy-red stems and deep rose-red buds that open to lighter pink flowers, giving the plant noticeably more color saturation than white or pale-pink types. Its dwarf, mounded habit fits well in containers, front-of-border plantings, and small residential gardens where larger gaura cultivars sprawl. Plant in full sun in lean, sharply drained soil, since wet or heavy soil quickly leads to crown rot in this species. Bloom is continuous from late spring through frost, and the reduced height means it rarely needs the midseason cutback larger gaura types require to stay tidy.

common_name: Summer's Swan Song Ironweed (Compact Narrowleaf Ironweed Cultivar)

planting.note: Set out nursery divisions in spring after frost danger has passed; this late-blooming selection is valued for extending the ironweed nectar season deep into fall.

directions: Summer's Swan Song is a narrowleaf ironweed selection bred for a later, longer bloom window than the species, carrying its threadlike, fine-textured foliage on a slightly taller, more upright frame before topping out with clouds of small magenta-purple flowers well into autumn. Plant in full sun in lean to average, well-drained soil; once established it needs very little supplemental water and tolerates both heat and short dry spells without wilting. The late nectar supply makes it valuable for migrating monarchs and other late-season pollinators when many other prairie perennials have already finished blooming. Cut the stems back in late winter before new growth emerges in spring.
sources: Mt. Cuba Center Trial Garden Notes
